# Doc-drift patterns — strings that MUST NOT appear in any tracked file
# outside `docs/adr/` (where they are allowed for historical context).
#
# Add an entry whenever you delete or rename a file, symbol, or image tag
# that the rest of the repo might still reference. CI enforces this on
# every push.
#
# One literal pattern per line. Lines starting with `#` are comments.
# Patterns are passed to `grep -F` (fixed-string), not regex.
#
# Maintenance: when an entry has been clean for ≥ 1 month after the last
# stale reference was removed, it's safe to delete the entry from this
# file too — the goal is to catch fresh drift, not maintain a memorial.

# 2026-05-19 — single-image refactor (ADR 0008 + ADR 0009)
# 2026-08-05: `build_image.sh` / `push_image.sh` entries retired — the
# personal-GCP Cloud Build script `06_build_image.sh` (2026-07-14, sanctioned
# by ADR 0016) legitimately carries the substring; the actually-removed
# laptop scripts remain covered by the two *_gpu_* patterns.
Dockerfile.gpu
GPU_CONTAINER.md
build_gpu_image.sh
push_gpu_image.sh

# Image tag rename. Patterns are bounded by `:` and `/` to avoid
# false positives on substrings like `sdfb-gpu-something`.
sdfb-gpu:
sdfb-gpu/

# 2026-05-21 — vllm_spike.py deleted (no local GPU; §11 Dataflow probe is the
# vLLM validation path). Catch any re-introduced reference.
vllm_spike

# 2026-05-21 — GCS model-layout convention moved from `{project}-models` to
# `{bucket}/synthetic/models/...` (matches the deploy workflows). The old
# token survives only in docs/adr/ (excluded from this scan) as superseded
# history; it must not reappear in live code/config/docs.
project}-models
project>-models

# 2026-08-05 — E2E analysis scripts consolidated under scripts/e2e/
# (WS8 follow-up). The old flat paths must not reappear; the new
# scripts/e2e/<name> paths do NOT match these fixed strings.
scripts/e2e_gcp_probe.py
scripts/e2e_validation_analysis.py
scripts/e2e_bundle_export.py
scripts/freetext_crosscheck.py

# 2026-06-30 — dispatch ENTRYPOINT (ADR 0009). Dataflow does NOT override the
# worker entrypoint; it appends FnAPI boot flags, so docker/entrypoint.sh
# dispatches boot vs launcher. The old (disproven) claim that Dataflow uses an
# explicit --entrypoint override and the image ENTRYPOINT is "irrelevant for
# workers" caused the sdk-0-0 CrashLoopBackOff — it must not reappear in live
# files (the ADR 0009 correction note, in docs/adr/, is excluded from the scan).
irrelevant for workers
